title: The linked material-to-Congress-confidence path varies by income and race/ethnicity
source_unit: US Census HTOPS April and June 2025 linked public-use respondents; subgroup cross-lags among retained SCRAMID matches

denominator.unit: linked respondents; subgroup valid n varies

observations.method: Inner join on SCRAMID; baseline EXPNS_DIF coded any difficulty versus not difficult; June TRUST2_CONGRESS coded high confidence as a great deal or quite a lot; estimates use April PWEIGHT0 and 80 successive-difference replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: This is a conditional precision diagnostic for a selected linked sample. The April weights are not documented as attrition-adjusted longitudinal weights, and no multiple-comparison or causal model is claimed.
observations.subgroup: Baseline household-income categories and combined race/ethnicity categories from the April HTOPS PUF.
observations.counterinterpretation: Differences can reflect selection, composition, prior institutional confidence, political identity, health, debt, local conditions, or reporting; subgroup contrast is not a mechanism estimate.

related_sources.claim: The all-linked HTOPS panel shows material persistence and movement alongside selected institutional judgments.
Full income and race/ethnicity subgroup estimates with replicate-weight standard errors.

boundary: This record narrows a same-respondent material-to-institutional-judgment comparison by subgroup. It does not measure attributed responsibility, civic action, vote, remedy, recovery, or causality, and it must not be interpreted as an attrition-adjusted national panel estimate.
